subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit soft-steer lifecycle beyond current boundary-based steer behavior, and should it be opt-in rather than changing the default queue contract?
rationale: The choice affects shared runtime semantics, message ordering, partial-output handling, channel UX, Codex/native runtime integration, and compatibility with existing steer, followup, collect, and interrupt modes.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with coverage for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Treat current boundary-based steer plus active-run admission fixes as the supported behavior and document that users should use interrupt when they want abort semantics.

options.title: Finish Narrow Admission First
options.body: Land or replace the PR 89238-style ordinary-message admission fix before deciding whether true pause/resume soft steer belongs in core.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Add a separate mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with coverage for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on active-run steering and adjacent reply-run lifecycle behavior that this decision must preserve.
